component.name: Apache Hop
component.description: Hop Orchestration Platform: visual data and metadata orchestration (pipelines and workflows) authored in a GUI and run on a local engine, a remote Hop Server, or Beam runners. Hop executes operator-authored pipelines that by design read/write files, query databases, call services, and run scripting/exec steps; it is not a sandbox and not a multi-tenant isolation boundary. Hop is operated as a single trust domain: the author, local operator, and Hop Server credential holders are all trusted, and the network-facing Hop Server and REST API are where untrusted actors can appear. Threat model ratified by the Hop PMC.

externalReferences.comment: Source threat model document; this file is a structured translation of it.

blueprints.name: Hop execution deployment
blueprints.description: Trust boundaries described by the threat model: a trusted author/operator drives the engine; a remote client reaching the Hop Server (embedded Jetty servlets) or the separate hop-rest JAX-RS API is the high-value network boundary; metadata/project files are parsed on load but only execute when run; the connection layer carries operator-configured credentials to external backends; variables are resolved by raw substitution and can carry untrusted data to sinks.

assets.name: Execution engine
assets.description: Runs operator-authored pipelines (.hpl) and workflows (.hwf), including transforms that touch files, databases, network, and scripting/exec steps with full host/JVM capability.

assets.name: Hop Server (servlet/HTTP)
assets.description: Embedded Jetty server whose servlets accept pipeline/workflow run requests over HTTP (/hop/execPipeline, /hop/addPipeline + /hop/startExec, /hop/registerPackage, ...). HTTP Basic auth is enabled by default but the only shipped credential is the publicly-known cluster/cluster, there is no per-endpoint authorization, and the Docker image binds 0.0.0.0:8080 with those defaults.

assets.name: Hop REST API (hop-rest)
assets.description: A distinct JAX-RS WAR exposing /api/v1/execute and /api/v1/metadata CRUD. It has no built-in authentication; auth is whatever the servlet container or reverse proxy provides.

assets.name: Pipeline/workflow and metadata files
assets.description: Unsigned XML (.hpl/.hwf) with no signature, provenance, or integrity check; loading parses them with a hardened XML parser, running them executes their steps. Connection passwords stored in them are only reversibly obfuscated by default.

assets.name: External backends (databases, files, cloud services)
assets.description: Operator-configured connection targets reached through bundled JDBC drivers and HTTP/REST/cloud transforms; responses are backend-controlled.

zones.name: Remote network clients
zones.description: Untrusted-capable clients of the Hop Server and REST API; bounded by whatever auth fronts the surface.

zones.name: Hop single trust domain
zones.description: The pipeline/workflow author, local operator, and any holder of Hop Server credentials, plus the engine/server/GUI they control; all trusted, with no isolation between pipelines or tenants.

zones.name: External backends
zones.description: Databases, file stores, and services the operator connects to; a network MITM between Hop and its backends is an in-scope adversary.

boundaries.name: Remote client to Hop Server / REST API

assumptions.description: Environment: a JVM and OS with full file and process access for exec/shell/scripting steps; network reachability to configured backends and the Hop Server listen interface; the system trust store for outbound TLS (the operator sets javax.net.ssl.keyStore where strict outbound TLS verification is required).
Pipeline/workflow definitions, connection configs, and metadata are trusted operator/author input; running an untrusted .hpl/.hwf is equivalent to running untrusted instructions.

Variables and parameters may be untrusted-capable: a Set Variables transform can copy an upstream row-stream value (or OS env / -D property) into a variable that is resolved by raw, unescaped substitution into SQL, paths, or shell bodies.

Out of scope: hop-website, docs, tests, assembly build mechanics (though the shipped default posture is an in-scope fact), bundled third-party JDBC driver CVEs, credential acquisition/rotation for backends, and multi-tenant isolation.

threats.name: Bypass of the Hop Server authentication gate
threats.description: The servlet Hop Server enables HTTP Basic authentication by default, gating every endpoint. A genuine implementation defect that lets an endpoint be reached without the configured credential, an authorization hole beyond the documented single /* role, or an XXE bypassing the hardened parser is a valid finding under the in-scope remote adversary.

threats.name: Remote code execution via an exposed Hop Server with the default credential
threats.description: The only shipped credential is the publicly-known cluster/cluster (pwd/hop.pwd), there is no per-endpoint authorization (any authenticated user can run/stop pipelines), and the Docker image binds 0.0.0.0:8080 with those defaults. An exposed deployment with the unchanged default credential (or enable_auth=false) gives remote pipeline execution, which is remote code execution. Changing the credential and restricting exposure is an operator responsibility.

threats.name: Unauthenticated pipeline execution via the exposed REST API
threats.description: The separate hop-rest deployable exposes /api/v1/execute and /api/v1/metadata CRUD with no built-in authentication; exposing it to an untrusted network without a fronting auth layer allows unauthenticated pipeline execution and metadata mutation. Access control is entirely the deployment's responsibility.

threats.name: Running an untrusted pipeline or workflow file
threats.description: Running an untrusted .hpl/.hwf is equivalent to executing untrusted instructions: there is no signature, provenance, or integrity check on these files, and an authored pipeline runs scripting/shell/SQL and touches files/network with full host capability by design (no SecurityManager; GraalJS with HostAccess.ALL; Rhino without a ClassShutter; Janino/UDJC compile arbitrary Java; Exec process/Shell run OS commands). Loading alone only parses; running executes.

threats.name: Injection via untrusted variable or parameter values
threats.description: Variables (${VAR}/%%VAR%%/$[hex]) are resolved by raw, unescaped string substitution and concatenated directly into SQL strings, file paths, and shell bodies; a value sourced from an untrusted upstream row (via Set Variables) or attacker-influenced OS env / -D property is an injection surface (SQL injection, path traversal, shell command construction). Parameterizing/escaping untrusted variables is the pipeline author's job. (The SQL row-stream value path uses PreparedStatement binding and is not the injection concern.)

threats.name: Recovery of default-obfuscated credentials at rest
threats.description: Connection passwords in metadata are by default only reversibly obfuscated, not encrypted: the built-in Hop encoder XORs against a hardcoded, publicly-known seed, and anyone with the file recovers the plaintext. Real confidentiality is opt-in via the AES2 encoder (AES-GCM with an operator-held key) or a secrets resolver (Vault, Azure Key Vault, Google Secret Manager). An exposed default-obfuscated metadata password is recoverable by design.

threats.name: Credential leakage through resolved URLs in debug logs
threats.description: No plaintext password is logged by default and decrypted DB passwords travel in a JDBC Properties object, not the URL; however, resolved JDBC/REST/HTTP URLs are logged at debug/detailed level without credential masking, so credentials an author embeds in a URL can leak. A credential leak in logs beyond this documented behavior would be a valid finding.

threats.name: Weakened outbound TLS verification and MITM exposure
threats.description: A network MITM between Hop and its backends or between client and server is an in-scope adversary. Hop Server TLS is available (Jetty sslConfig with a JKS keystore) but off by default; ServerConnectionManager installs a process-global default SSLContext that skips CA-chain/hostname validation (date-only) when javax.net.ssl.keyStore is unset; several transforms offer opt-in ignoreSsl/trustAllCertificates switches (defaulting to verification on). Enabling TLS and setting the keystore is an operator responsibility.

threats.name: XXE bypassing the hardened XML parser
threats.description: Pipeline/workflow/metadata files are parsed through a secure DocumentBuilderFactory with external general/parameter entities and external DTD loading disabled and FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING on, mitigating XXE file-read/SSRF and entity expansion; the same secure parser is used by the Hop Server remote-add endpoints. An XXE that bypasses this hardened parser is a valid finding.

threats.name: Vulnerabilities in bundled third-party JDBC drivers
threats.description: A CVE in a packaged driver (lib-jdbc bundles redshift, clickhouse, h2, mssql, vertica, crate, monetdb, jt400, snowflake, derby, duckdb, hsqldb, postgresql, sqlite, mysql) is a dependency/supply-chain matter, not a Hop defect; Hop's job is to call them correctly.

trustBoundaries.name: Hop Server / REST API trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: The high-value boundary: a network client requests pipeline/workflow execution. Authentication, transport security, and who can run what live here; the separate REST API is a second network surface with no built-in auth of its own.

trustBoundaries.name: Connection-layer trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: Carries operator-configured credentials to external backends; responses are backend-controlled and a network MITM is in scope. Outbound JDBC TLS is driver-delegated; HTTP/REST/cloud transforms use the JVM trust store unless given a per-transform truststore.

controls.name: HTTP Basic authentication on by default
controls.description: The servlet Hop Server enables HTTP Basic authentication by default (enable_auth defaults to true), gating every endpoint so a fully unauthenticated client is rejected. Caveat: the shipped credential is the publicly-known default, and a single /* role gate means no per-endpoint authorization.

controls.name: XXE-hardened XML parsing
controls.description: Pipeline/workflow/metadata files are parsed through a secure DocumentBuilderFactory (XmlParserFactoryProducer) with external entities and external DTD loading disabled and FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING on; the Hop Server remote-add endpoints use the same secure parser.

controls.name: Lock down the Hop Server
controls.description: Change the default cluster/cluster credential, do not expose the remote-execution API to an untrusted network, restrict who can submit runs, and be aware the Docker image binds 0.0.0.0:8080 with the default credential.

controls.name: Front the REST API with authentication
controls.description: Do not expose the hop-rest REST API without a fronting authentication layer (reverse proxy or container auth); it has none of its own.

controls.name: Protect credentials at rest
controls.description: Enable the AES2 encoder (HOP_PASSWORD_ENCODER_PLUGIN=AES2 with HOP_AES_ENCODER_KEY or HOP_AES_ENCODER_KEY_FILE) and/or a secrets resolver (HashiCorp Vault, Azure Key Vault, Google Secret Manager); never commit default-obfuscated credentials to version control.

controls.name: Avoid embedding credentials in URLs
controls.description: Resolved JDBC/REST/HTTP URLs are logged at debug/detailed level without credential masking, so operators should avoid in-URL credentials.

controls.name: Enable TLS and strict outbound verification
controls.description: Serve the Hop Server over HTTPS via the sslConfig block of hop-server.xml (TLS is off by default), use TLS for sensitive backends, and set javax.net.ssl.keyStore to avoid the relaxed process-global TLS trust manager.

controls.name: Run pipelines from trusted authors only
controls.description: Do not source connection config or pipeline/metadata files from untrusted input; only run pipelines from trusted authors, since running an untrusted .hpl/.hwf is equivalent to executing untrusted instructions.

controls.name: Treat scripting/exec/SQL steps as code and parameterize untrusted variables
controls.description: Parameterize or escape any variable that may carry untrusted data before it reaches SQL strings, file paths, or shell bodies; the resolver does not escape.

controls.name: Populate the Janino code-exclusion deny-list if desired
controls.description: The opt-in, default-empty substring deny-list (JaninoCheckerUtil + codeExclusions.xml) covers only the three Janino-based steps and blocks nothing out of the box; operators can populate it to block named constructs (e.g. System.exit, Runtime.exec) in those steps.
